admin_account_lead: How you sign in, and where you are signed in.
admin_backup_confirm: This replaces the database and all configuration with the contents of this backup. What is there now is kept, in case this is a mistake. Continue?
admin_backup_damaged: This backup is damaged: part of it is not what its own manifest says it should be. Nothing was changed.
admin_backup_download_lead: One file with the database and every configuration document in it, encrypted with the password you choose here. Keep both — the file is useless without the password, and nobody can recover it for you.
admin_backup_inspected: This backup was taken on {when} and contains {count} items. Nothing has been changed.
admin_backup_lead: Everything this install holds, in one file you can take away — and the way back from one.
admin_backup_newer_build: This backup was written by a newer version of this software than the one running here. Update first, then restore it.
admin_backup_no_manifest: This file is not a backup of this software.
admin_backup_no_password: Enter the password this backup was made with.
admin_backup_not_an_archive: This file is not a backup at all.
admin_backup_password_hint: At least {count} characters. It is the only thing protecting a copy of the whole database.
admin_backup_restore_lead: Looking inside a backup changes nothing, so do that first if you are not sure which file this is. Restoring replaces the database and the configuration; what is there now is kept on the server rather than deleted.
admin_backup_restored: Restored the backup from {when}. What was here before has been kept on the server.
admin_backup_too_large: This file is larger than this install will accept.
admin_backup_unexpected_contents: This backup contains something this version will not restore. Nothing was changed.
admin_backup_wrong_password: That password does not open this backup — or the file is damaged. There is no way to tell which.
admin_kick_caveat: Linking Kick proves who you are and shows the account publicly. Reading your Kick videos and live status is not implemented yet.
admin_lead: The place the site is run from.
admin_link_token_warning: The token is sent to this site and stored encrypted. Paste one you can revoke.
admin_linked_accounts_lead: Accounts you have linked. One link serves signing in, the feeds this site reads, and the links shown on your public page.
admin_linked_checked_broken: That account could not be used. It has to be connected again.
admin_linked_checked_working: That account is connected and working.
admin_nothing_here_body: Accounts and sign-in work. The pages that edit the site — links, feed sources, the calendar — are still being built.
admin_people_last_owner: This is the only owner. Promote somebody else first.
admin_people_lead: Everyone with an account on this site.
admin_people_yourself: You cannot change your own role. Ask another owner or administrator.
admin_sessions_lead: One entry per browser. Ending one signs that browser out immediately.
admin_sign_in_methods_lead: Any of these signs you in to this same account. You cannot remove the last one.
admin_unlink_last: This is your only way to sign in, so it cannot be removed.
admin_youtube_caveat: Linking YouTube records your channel and shows it publicly. Your videos already appear from YouTube’s public feed, with or without the link.
auth_claimable: Nobody administers this site yet, so the first account to sign in becomes its owner.
auth_sign_in_lead: Signing in uses an account you already have. This site never sees your password.
auth_unavailable_body: No sign-in provider is configured on this installation. Whoever runs it has to set one up before anyone can sign in.
auth_unavailable_title: Signing in is not set up
chat_empty: No messages yet — chat appears here while the stream is live.
error_not_found_body: That page does not exist, or it has moved.
error_unexpected_body: Something went wrong at our end. Trying again may be enough.
home_lead: A self-hosted site for content creators. This install is not configured yet.
metrics_coverage_lead: {measured} platform(s) report their own numbers; {planned} are configured and not read yet. Each one says below what it is waiting for — usually the creator's account being linked.
metrics_derived: Worked out from the posts this site has fetched, not reported by the platform.
metrics_double_counted: Somebody who follows on two platforms is counted twice here.
metrics_lead: Every platform's numbers in one place. Only you can see this page.
metrics_none: Nothing to show yet. Add a source on the feed settings, or link an account so a platform will report its own numbers.
metrics_partial: Covers only what this site has read, not the whole channel.
metrics_platform_none: No numbers from this one yet.
metrics_third_party: From a third party that collects these numbers, not from the platform itself.
